In local SEO for craft workshops and service businesses, the main temptation is to quickly roll out pages for every city and service. But local visibility built on weak pages creates risk, not a sustainable structure.

- A geo page should pass an indexing gate. The minimum logic: is there demand for the service-plus-region combination; are there actual jobs completed or evidence of presence; is there enough unique material; has the page become outdated; is there a resource to maintain it. What matters is not the automation of generation, but the ability to stop publication of a page that has no substantive foundation.

- Structured data is useful when it reflects the real local structure of the business. Service, Organization, BreadcrumbList, FAQPage, and address data should be assembled from a single profile, not manually copied into every page. Otherwise, the slightest change in address, phone number, or service set creates desynchronization between the text, schema, and contact blocks.

- Content architecture affects the quality of local pages no less than keywords do. If prices, regions, proof of work, and FAQs are scattered across random text inserts, the site quickly becomes difficult to audit. If the data is canonicalized and validated, local SEO stops being a set of manual edits and becomes a manageable system.

What criterion do you use to decide whether a local page is ready to be indexed or should be kept out of the search results?
